facts.title: Discovery and alternative activation
facts.fact: Ordinary discovery scans PBS root *.txt only, matches exact base or base_ suffix after longest-base ordering. Gen5–8 subdirectories are author alternatives, not simultaneous or automatically active registries. Explicit facility Trainers/Pokemon paths bypass generic basename discovery. A copied backup remains subject to current schema, dependencies, code and settings; changing its directory name does not recompute loaded settings constants.

facts.title: Lexical and schema collection
facts.fact: First-line BOM removal, physical comment/blank skip and subsequent first-# suffix deletion precede ordinary attribute collection. A space followed by # within ordinary section becomes invalid empty attribute, unlike specialized prepped-line loops. Ordinary repeated attributes overwrite; ^ fields accumulate; valid unknown schema attributes are ignored. Fixed schema ignores excess tail, q consumes preprocessed original string. Escaped-quote marker removal is positional; ordinary CSV quotation is not a general unquote guarantee.

facts.title: Registry identity and incomplete compile
facts.fact: String IDs normalize to Symbol, comparisons and enum membership are exact; no STICK→LEEK or VICEGRIP→VISEGRIP alias is supplied by generic registry. get unknown raises; try_get unknown/nil returns nil, but wrong types fail validation. Direct register replaces same key; ordinary compiler duplicate gate rejects before second registration. Clear and successful prefix registrations occur before whole-table validation/save. Failure does not itself undo earlier in-memory registrations.

facts.title: Four schema families and defaults
facts.fact: Each actual author field is parsed by its declared schema. Type references and Move Type/Target and Item Move are validated against the current registered dependency, not the English display label. Missing and explicit zero/false remain distinct. All complete defaults and field interpretations are in field-contracts.json; every present and omitted field of all 7704 primary path-records binds that contract in record-field-ledger.json.

facts.title: Move validation and effect identity
facts.fact: Status with positive power rejects before current record registration; Physical/Special with zero or omitted power warns and becomes Status. FunctionCode is author text and is not validated against a move-effect implementation at compile time. Factory resolves exact function name (digit prefix Effect); lawful absent effect falls back to Unimplemented. Missing/nil function uses None, not arbitrary empty or malformed name. Source and formal lawful missing-effect examples already preserve different status-failure and ordinary-damage branches.

facts.title: Types, generation and combat categories
facts.fact: All default19 and Gen5 18 rows read; Gen6/7/8 equal default. QMARKS is pseudo and neutral in supplied table, not universally unusable. Gen5 lacks FAIRY and retains STEEL resistance to DARK/GHOST. Each defending type checks weaknesses before resistances before immunities; generic Effectiveness.calculate multiplies all supplied defending arguments without deduplication, while ordinary battler type collection supplies its own deduplicated types. Per-move category switch is independent of author backup; old-category mode queries current type special flag. Optional Shadow input is a separate activation condition.

facts.title: Ability data versus callback behavior
facts.fact: All1122 per-path ability records bind ID/name/description/Flags. Data descriptions are display strings; callback lookup uses effective ability identity at each actual caller. FasterEggHatching is present only on the explicitly read flagged rows (MAGMAARMOR/FLAMEBODY, plus default/Gen8 STEAMENGINE). Neither a plain description nor registration proves handler activation. MERCILESS reads target poison; wording it poisoned is not a source admission rule. Gen5/6/7 availability164/191/233 and current267 do not imply mechanic-generation changes.

facts.title: Compile, save, startup reload and failure
facts.fact: Main loads core messages, plugins, Compiler.main, then Game.initialize. Compiler.main is debug-gated, uses missing required data/full flag/CTRL/import and integer-second maximum text>=maximum data time trigger; deletes listed data before full stage if triggered. Successful stage saves table/message outputs; ordinary startup GameData.load_all replaces registries. No Ruby/serialized load was run here.

facts.title: Existing objects and save-game reload
facts.fact: Game.load(save_data) applies saved values/maps rather than recompiling or calling GameData.load_all. Pokemon::Move holds ID/PP/PPUp but queries data fields and totalPP live by ID. Battle::Move snapshots name/function/power/type/category/accuracy/target/priority/effectChance and clones flags at construction; its totalPP may delegate to realMove unless positive explicit override. AIMove wraps this existing battle object, sets calcType and moldBreaker during setup and uses skill-dependent own handlers/callbacks. Registry reload cannot be generalized to refresh all existing battle snapshots, caches or old data instances.

facts.fact: Generic writer selects suffix paths from current registry entries, emits BOM/CRLF and schema properties. Type/Ability/Move/Item omissions use constructor/default/property policies; Item false Consumable for nonimportant must be written, sale-half/BP1/use0 may omit. Author text and metadata do not prove translated text, pixels, host availability or byte round-trip.

value.premises: Fixed R, standard GameData objects, no plugin overrides or external writes; source-stage reasoning only. Actual Map051 tileset/area/event binding and runtime absent.

facts.fact: Dungeon construction precedes generate. Width/height below20 are node counts scaled by cell size plus screen buffer. Snap parameter odd-field writes can fail before generation because standard fields have no writer; no generator seed consumption or original map rewrite reached. All four present parameter×tileset pairs use even10/10/2, so that particular gate is skipped.

Choose parameter rng_seed, else global pending seed S, else system new seed, by Ruby truthiness; then clear S, then reseed global Random. Parameter priority still clears S. No local independent random stream or restoration is introduced. Failure evaluating selection may precede clear; failure in reseed follows clear. Host random implementation/sequence is unverified.

Negative usable drawing width or height returns normally after seed selection/clear/reseed. Otherwise redraw loop clears layout and reruns stages but never reseeds or clears the stored room-rectangle list; random consumption continues from the prior prefix. No retry bound or termination proof.

Maze obtains visitable nodes before random starting-node selection and then reads its x/y. Empty visitable set fails before direction shuffling and subsequent room/decorative draws. No exact positive or zero random-channel consumption is inferred for native empty sample.

Registered Dungeon flag gates receiver. Tileset/parameter lookup and Dungeon construction precede generate. Only after generate returns does original map receive width then height then data resize then tile writes. Generate-time exception does not reach these original-map writes; prior seed/random prefix remains.

Tile conversion traverses x, then y, then layer; ignore retains old value, none writes0, large decoration draws four mapped choices and writes2×2 offsets. Exceptions retain already-written original-map prefix; no rollback/ensure. Tile random draws follow layout-generation draws on global channel.

Placement clones stored rectangles, filters inadequate sizes, returns nil if none, else attempts1000 room/x/y choices. Checks occupied spacing only, not current floor terrain; success appends all event cells then returns bottom-left coordinate. Retained prior-redraw rectangles therefore remain conditional candidates; no actual bad seed or placement observed.

Each of100 rounds resets failed=false and occupied cells. Any event failure sets failed and aborts that round, leaving already-moved events. Player failure continues without setting failed. Only final failed=true raises. If all rounds have successful events but failed player, receiver returns normally with last event locations and old player_new_x/y. Successful player placement writes x then y. No transfer flag is set here and no rollback occurs; outer runtime-event creation and later subscriber effects require actual caller receipt.

Explicit2×2 node fixture with cell10×10 and antiring, no fixed seed and pending S, given successful constructor/lookup and legal surrounding buffers: every candidate x/y is an edge, so all four are rejected by antiring at137–138 and visitable set is empty. Maze start sample at168 yields no element, first coordinate read169 fails; direction shuffle177, add connections and spawn rooms are not reached. Whole-area no-room fallback464 cannot rescue earlier failure. Generate already selected S, cleared S and globally reseeded; callback map width/height/resize1073 onward and player temp writes are not reached. Native empty sample random-channel advancement is UNVERIFIED; only concrete reached prefix is retained. Current supplied5×4/full records do not assert this failure.

Four distinct density-zero cases, each conditioned on successful earlier stages and its corresponding decoration mapping existing. Processing order: large floor at917–918 divides drawable maxWidth×maxHeight by floor_decoration_large_density; small floor933–934 divides usable_width×usable_height by floor_decoration_density; large void942–943 divides width×height by void_decoration_large_density; small void958–959 divides width×height by void_decoration_density. Integer denominator0 fails before that category coordinate draws. Missing mapping skips its category and its division. Earlier layout/walls/patches/categories may have consumed randomness and changed internal layout; S is already cleared/global random reseeded.
